title: Regional Token Flow & Capacity Slack Simulator (hosted API)
body:
SPREADSHEET: Regional token-level COGS and slack simulator (per 1M tokens basis)

Columns: Model Family | Variant | Region | Avg Seq len | GPU-hrs per 1M tokens | Infra $/GPU-hr | Infra $/1M tokens | Energy $/1M | License $/1M | NW+Ops $/1M | Total COGS $/1M | Cost per 1k tokens $ | Suggested price per 1k tokens $ | Gross margin % | Recommended capacity slack % | Routing note

Small-embed-model | embed-1.2b | us-west1 | 64 | 0.02 | 3.50 | 0.07 | 0.02 | 0 | 8.00 | 8.09 | 0.0081 | 0.25 | 96.8% | 12% | embeddings lane; high cache hit expected

Notes on table and assumptions:
- GPU-hrs per 1M tokens: estimated from internal benchmarking (continuous batching + KV cache enabled). Values represent typical production inference with our serving runtime and conservative request mix.
- Infra $/GPU-hr: blended region list price (cloud + amortized reserved fraction).
- Energy and NW+Ops are rough engineering ops estimates: energy = measured power cost per-hour * GPU-hr; NW+Ops covers egress, bandaid SRE, scheduling overhead and token accounting.
- License $/1M applied only to vendor-licensed large models (examples shown), set to zero for permissive open models.
- Cost per 1k tokens = Total COGS $/1M / 1000. Suggested price uses a goal margin band and market reference.

Scenario toggles (what to flip in the simulator):
- Quantization switch: reduce GPU-hrs per 1M by 30–60% depending on model; impacts license risk and quality.
- Cache hit rate: for chat/assistant traffic, increasing prefix/KV cache from 0% -> 50% reduces effective tokens served and GPU-hrs proportionally.
- Batch window: expanding batching window increases tokens/M GPU-hr (improves efficiency) but adds latency tail; simulate 0ms / 20ms / 100ms windows.
- Reserved capacity fraction: move infra $/GPU-hr down by committed discount when reserve fraction increases.

Sensitivity insights (quick takeaways):
- Mid-sized decoder models (7–13B) are where marginal unit-econ improvements buy the most delta per-dollar. Shaving 0.05 GPU-hrs/M on 13B yields >$25/M saving across common request mix.
- Licensed 70B variants dominate COGS because of license line and higher GPU usage; they should be served only for clear quality needs or via dedicated/reserved contracts.
- Regions with higher infra rates (APAC) require more aggressive routing/quantization and higher slack targets to avoid burst spot-price exposure.
- Embeddings remain highly favorable for caching and precomputation; pushing more to cached vectors reduces hosted API marginals significantly.

Recommended immediate actions and owners:
- (OPT-430) Add a dedicated simulator tab that toggles quantization, cache-hit, and reserve fraction; owner: Mateo Silva; due: 2025-02-28.
- (ENG-804) Benchmark 13B quant-8bit variant at 256 seq and produce a reproducible GPU-hrs/M measurement; owner: Aisha Khan; due: 2025-02-14.
- (PRODUCT-212) Draft a routing policy to prefer low-cost quantized variants for non-SLA routes and surface explicit fallback SLOs; owner: Riley Chen; due: 2025-03-07.
- (FIN-118) Model 3-year reserve commit scenarios (25/50/75%) and publish blended infra $/GPU-hr curves into the workbook; owner: Priya Kapoor; due: 2025-03-14.

Open questions and TODOs (notes to reviewers):
- Validate license amortization cadence for 70B models (monthly vs per-M token) with legal/partnerships.
- Decide guardrail for routing: what percentage of traffic can be automatically downgraded to quantized variants without product sign-off?
- Confirm acceptable latency increase for 20ms extra batching windows for consumer vs enterprise plans.

Quick summary (1 paragraph):
This simulator is a lightweight per-1M-token workbench that lets product, infra and finance toggle quantization, cache hit-rate, batch windows and reserve fraction to understand marginal COGS and margin impact by model and region. Initial runs show that optimizing mid-sized models and routing APAC traffic to quantized variants yields the biggest near-term unit-econ wins; licensed 70B remains a high-cost uplifter that should be constrained to reserved/dedicated capacity or premium routes.
